data.long_meaning: The name Joniel is derived from the Hebrew word 'Yonah', which means 'dove'. In the Bible, Yonah is the name of a prophet who was called by God to go to the city of Nineveh and warn the inhabitants to repent of their sins. The name Joniel can be interpreted as 'God is gracious' or 'God has granted'. The name Joniel carries the meaning “God is gracious” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Hebrew, Greek. Parents who choose Joniel usually hope their child will grow to embody god is gracious and live with faith, good character and purpose.

data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Joniel total 2, giving a life-path number of 2. Number 2 is linked with Moon and with the qualities of harmony, sensitivity and partnership.

data.cultural_impact: The name Joniel has a rich historical and cultural significance for Christians as it is derived from the biblical character Jonah, who is known for his remarkable obedience and faith in God, despite his initial reluctance to follow God’s command. The name is often given to boys as a reminder of this extraordinary story of faith and devotion, and it has been popular among Christians for centuries.
data.spiritual_significance: The name Joniel carries a deep spiritual significance as it reminds us of the power of God’s love and patience, as well as the importance of obedience and faith. The name can inspire us to follow God’s will, no matter how challenging it may be, and to trust in His divine plan for our lives. It also serves as a reminder of God’s grace and mercy, as conveyed in the name's meaning 'God is gracious' or 'God has granted'. Overall, the name Joniel is a powerful reminder of the power and beauty of the Christian faith and the infinite love and grace of God.

historical_references.reference: Joniel was a popular name in medieval Spain for both males and females. A common belief was that the name was derived from Jonas in the Bible, who was swallowed by a whale and later rescued.

Another theory suggests that the name Joniel originated from Joanella, a diminutive form of the name Johanna, which was popular during the Late Middle Ages in Europe. The name Joniel may have been a masculine variant of Johanna.
